The claim is true, with one correction: each launch leaves two empty folders, not one, and opening a new blank project leaves one more. All 147 folders in `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/projects` are empty, and the Home page skips them on purpose. The fix belongs in JusPrin's own autosave code, so no OrcaSlicer file has to change.

## What I checked

- **The folders are empty.** Each of the 147 holds five empty subfolders and an empty `lock` file. None has a `HEAD` file, which is the pointer to a saved version, and together they take 0 bytes.
- **Two per launch.** I compared folder creation times with today's app logs. The 14:58, 15:37 and 15:44 launches each made one folder when the shell started. Each made a second one about five seconds later, when Orca's startup "New Project" gave the blank project a new ID.
- **Why it happens.** The `ProjectAutosave` constructor and every project switch call `adopt_project()`. That builds a `ProjectVersionStore`, and its constructor creates the whole folder tree and takes the lock right away ([ProjectVersionStore.cpp:404](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:404)). Nothing deletes the folder if nothing is ever saved into it.
- **Why Home doesn't show them.** `projects()` and `resume_latest()` skip any folder that has no `HEAD` ([ProjectAutosave.cpp:752](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:752)).

## Proposal: create the folder on the first save

`ProjectVersionStore` would no longer create anything on disk when it opens a project ID that has no folder yet. Its in-memory state would just be empty: no saved version, no history. A private `ensure_created()` would make the folders and take the lock the first time something is written. That happens in five methods: `freeze`, `publish_document`, `pin`, `record_operation` and `begin_chat_restore`. A project ID that already has a folder opens exactly as it does today.

This fixes the cause rather than cleaning up afterwards. It also covers crashes and killed test runs, which a cleanup step in the destructor would miss. The change stays inside `ProjectVersionStore`, so the roughly 25 `m_store->` calls in `ProjectAutosave` don't change.

**One behaviour change.** Today, if two JusPrin windows open the same 3MF file, the second fails as soon as it adopts the project ("project is open in another JusPrin instance"). With this change it fails at its first save instead, a few seconds later. I think that's acceptable.

**Tests.**
- A unit test: opening a store for a new ID creates no folder; the first `freeze` and `publish` create it and take the lock; and a second store on the same ID still fails to lock.
- An end-to-end check with the shell test harness and its own data folder: launch, quit and relaunch without editing, and expect no new folders. Then add an object, and expect one folder that Home lists.

## Decisions for you

1. **The 147 that already exist.** If `jusprin-newui` hasn't reached testers yet, I'd delete them by hand on your machine and add no cleanup code. If it has, I'd add a sweep when the app starts. The sweep would delete folders that have no `HEAD` and whose lock it can take. It has a small race with a second JusPrin window that is starting at the same moment.
2. **The `jusprin/recovery` folder.** It holds 452 more per-project folders. Each has a `state.json` and a `recovery.json`, and none has been written since 2026-09-29. The current code only reads them, and only as an extra copy of the chat state. They could be removed in the same change.

## Something else you should know

The 15:37 and 15:44 logs show 8 folders that did have a `HEAD`. They were older-format projects the current code could not read; the errors were missing JSON keys such as `regions`, `openedFrom` and `changeSeq`. Those folders were gone by the time I looked, after 15:47. Your quote says the other 147 were "left alone", so I assume whichever session wrote it deleted those 8 on purpose. That's an assumption: I didn't check which session did it.

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

JusPrin no longer leaves an empty folder behind for blank projects. A project's folder now appears only when something is first saved to it. On a fresh test data folder, two launches used to leave six empty folders beside the one real project; now only the real project is there. The changes are uncommitted on `jusprin-newui`.

**Cleanup on your machine.** I moved the 147 empty project folders and all 452 recovery folders to `~/.Trash/jusprin-cleanup-2026-10-20`, so you can still restore them. I left one folder alone because the JusPrin window you had open was using it. That window has since saved real work into it (versions from 15:47 to 16:04), so it's a real project now. The window also created one more empty folder before it quit, and I moved that one too.

**Code changes:**
- **Folder on first save** ([ProjectVersionStore.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp)). Opening a project no longer creates its folder. The first write creates the folder and takes the lock that keeps two JusPrin windows off the same project. That write refuses if another JusPrin window saved the same project in the meantime.
- **Fresh-install crash, caught by testing.** With no saved projects, the `jusprin/projects` folder doesn't exist at all, and the Home page's project list crashed the app. It now treats a missing folder as "no projects yet", as the two other places that read this folder already do ([ProjectAutosave.cpp:749](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:749)).
- **Recovery code removed.** The current app never wrote to the recovery folders; it only read old copies from them when opening a project. I removed that code, its setting and its tests, and updated two docs and three comments that mentioned it.

**Tests:**
- I added two checks to the shell test harness: no empty folder after a fresh start, and none after a restart. Both failed before the fix and pass after it.
- I added three version-store checks to the workspace harness. Before the fix, two failed and the third couldn't run, because the old code locks a project as soon as it opens it. All three pass now, and the full workspace harness passes with 0 failures.
- All 380 Agent unit tests pass, and so does the full default shell harness (563 checks).
- My last edit, which removed a stale comment in `ProjectStateDocument.hpp`, came after the final build. It only touches a comment, so I didn't rebuild for it.

**Something you should know.** Another session committed `beba691b80` ("Open the All settings panel on the whole project") in this same checkout while I worked. It only touched Agent page web files, so it doesn't overlap my changes.

Should I commit this?
commit it
